Lark Cheatsheet

Basic Syntax

  • rule_name: definition - Define a rule
  • TERMINAL: /regex/ - Define a terminal using regex
  • ?rule_name: ... - Inline rule (keeps the tree flat)
  • _rule_name: ... - Ignore rule (hides from the tree)
  • // comment or # comment

Operators

  • a | b - Match a OR b
  • a? - Optional (0 or 1)
  • a* - Zero or more
  • a+ - One or more
  • a ~ n - Exactly n times
  • a ~ n..m - Between n and m times
  • [a b] - Maybe (optional) group
  • (a b) - Grouping

Common Terminals (from common.lark)

You can import these directly: %import common.INT

Numbers

  • INT: Integer (e.g., 42)
  • SIGNED_INT: Integer with optional sign (+42, -42)
  • FLOAT: Floating point number
  • DECIMAL: Decimal number
  • NUMBER: INT or FLOAT

Strings & Names

  • ESCAPED_STRING: "Double quoted string"
  • CNAME: Valid Python identifier (e.g., my_var)
  • WORD: Any sequence of letters

Whitespace & Comments

  • WS: Whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines)
  • WS_INLINE: Inline whitespace (spaces, tabs)
  • SH_COMMENT: # Shell style comment
  • C_COMMENT: /* C style comment */
  • CPP_COMMENT: // C++ style comment
